parts.title: Bovids
parts.article:
(A) The family of mammals called bovids belongs to the Artiodactyl class, which also includes giraffes. Bovids are a highly diverse group consisting of 137 species, some of which are man’s most important domestic animals.

(B) Bovids are well represented in most parts of Eurasia and Southeast Asian islands, but they are by far the most numerous and diverse in the latter. Some species of bovid are solitary, but others live in large groups with complex social structures. Although bovids have adapted to a wide range of habitats, from arctic tundra to deep tropical forest, the majority of species favour open grassland, scrub or desert. This diversity of habitat is also matched by great diversity in size and form: at one extreme is the royal antelope of West Africa, which stands a mere 25 cm at the shoulder; at the other, the massively built bison of North America and Europe, growing to a shoulder height of 2.2m.

(C) Despite differences in size and appearance, bovids are united by the possession of certain common features. All species are ruminants, which means that they retain undigested food in their stomachs, and regurgitate it as necessary. Bovids are almost exclusively herbivorous. Typically, their teeth are highly modified for browsing and grazing: grass or foliage is cropped with the upper lip and lower incisors (the upper incisors are usually absent), and then ground down by the cheek teeth. As well as having cloven, or split hooves, the males of all bovid species and the females of most carry horns. Bovid horns have bony cores covered in a sheath of horny material that is constantly renewed from within; they are unbranched and never shed. They vary in shape and size: the relatively simple horns of a large Indian buffalo may measure around 4 m from tip to tip along the outer curve, while the various gazelles have horns with a variety of elegant curves.

(D) Five groups, or sub-families, may be distinguished: Bovinae, Antelope, Caprinae, Cephalophinae and Antilocapridae. The sub-family Bovinae comprises most of the larger bovids, including the African bongo, nilgai, eland, bison and cattle. Unlike most other bovids, they are all non-territorial. The ancestors of the various species of domestic cattle (such as banteng, gaur, yak and water buffalo) are generally rare and endangered in the wild, while the auroch (the ancestor of the domestic cattle of Europe) is extinct.

(E) The term ‘antelope’ is not a very precise zoological name – it is used to loosely describe a number of bovids that have followed different lines of development. Antelopes are typically long-legged, fast-running species, often with long horns that may be laid along the back when the animal is in full flight. There are two main sub-groups of antelope: Hippotraginae, which includes the oryx and the addax, and Antilopinae, which generally contains slighter and more graceful animals such as gazelle and the springbok. Antelopes are mainly grassland species, but many have adapted to flooded grasslands: pukus, waterbucks and lechwes are all good at swimming, usually feeding in deep water, while the sitatunga has long, splayed hooves that enable it to walk freely on swampy ground.

(F) The sub-family Caprinae includes the sheep and the goat, together with various relatives such as the goral and the tahr. Most are woolly or have long hair. Several species, such as wild goats, chamois and ibex, are agile cliff and mountain-dwellers. Tolerance of extreme conditions is most marked in this group: barbary and bighorn sheep have adapted to arid deserts, while Rocky Mountain sheep survive high up in mountains and musk oxen in arctic tundra.

(G) The duiker of Africa belongs to the Cephalophinae sub-family. It is generally small and solitary, often living in thick forest. Although mainly feeding on grass and leaves, some duikers – unlike most other bovids – are believed to eat insects and feed on dead animal carcasses, and even to kill small animals.

(H) The pronghorn is the sole survivor of a New World sub-family of herbivorous ruminants, the Antilocapridae in North America. It is similar in appearance and habits to the Old World antelope. Although greatly reduced in numbers since the arrival of Europeans, and the subsequent enclosure of grasslands, the pronghorn is still found in considerable numbers throughout North America, from Washington State to Mexico. When alarmed by the approach of wolves or other predators, hairs on the pronghorn’s rump stand erect, so showing and emphasising the white patch there. At this signal, the whole herd gallops off at speed of over 60 km per hour.

Questions 1-3
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 1-3 on your answer sheet.

Q1 In which region is the biggest range of bovids to be found?

  • A Africa
  • B Eurasia
  • C North America
  • D South-east Asia

Q2 Most bovids have a preference for living in

  • A isolation.
  • B small groups.
  • C tropical forest.
  • D wide open spaces.

Q3 Which of the following features do all bovids have in common?

  • A Their horns are shed
  • B They have upper incisors
  • C They store food in the body
  • D Their hooves are undivided
Questions 4-8
List of sub-families
Look at the following characteristics (Question 4-8) and the list of sub-families below.
Match each characteristic with the correct sub-family, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter, A, B, C or D, in boxes 4-8 on your answer sheet.
NB You may use any letter more than once.
1
4 can endure very harsh environments
5 includes the ox and the cow
6 may supplement its diet with meat
7 can usually move at speed
8 does not defend a particular area of land

  • B Bovinae

  • D Cephalophinae
Question 9-13
Answer the questions below.
Choose NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 9-13 on your answer sheet.

10 Which species of Bovinae has now died out?

reference:
Q1

解析 文章明确说明牛科动物在欧亚大陆和东南亚岛屿都有分布，但在后者（the latter，也就是东南亚）数量最多且种类最丰富。

干扰 你可能看到Eurasia就选了B，但没有注意到后面有一个表示对比的“the latter（后者）”，这才是数量最多的地方。

句子 Bovids are well represented in most parts of Eurasia and Southeast Asian islands, but they are by far the most numerous and diverse in the latter.

Q2

解析 原文提到大部分（the majority）物种偏好开阔的草原、灌木丛或沙漠，这就完美对应了选项里的广阔开阔空间（wide open spaces）。

干扰 你可能看到arctic tundra或tropical forest就想选C，但这只是它们“能适应的范围”，并不是“大部分偏好”的地方。

句子 Although bovids have adapted to a wide range of habitats, from arctic tundra to deep tropical forest, the majority of species favour open grassland, scrub or desert.

Q3

解析 所有种类的牛科动物都会在胃里保留未消化的食物，这就对应了选项中的“在体内储存食物（store food in the body）”。

干扰 你可能会被干扰项A或B骗到，但原文明确说了它们的角是“不脱落的（never shed）”，并且“通常没有上门牙（upper incisors are usually absent）”，千万别记反了。

句子 All species are ruminants, which means that they retain undigested food in their stomachs, and regurgitate it as necessary.

Q4

解析 原文直接点出Caprinae这个亚科对极端条件的耐受力（Tolerance of extreme conditions）是最强的，也就是能忍受极其恶劣的环境。

干扰 你可能被具体列举的沙漠或高山迷惑了双眼，但这些地形都只是用来举例说明这个亚科具有强大的“耐受恶劣环境”的能力。

句子 The sub-family Caprinae includes the sheep and the goat, together with various relatives such as the goral and the tahr. / Tolerance of extreme conditions is most marked in this group: barbary and bighorn sheep have adapted to arid deserts, while Rocky Mountain sheep survive high up in mountains and musk oxen in arctic tundra.

Q5

解析 原文在列举Bovinae亚科包括的动物时，最后提到了cattle（牛），这完全等同于题目里的ox and cow。

干扰 你可能不知道cattle就是涵盖ox和cow的统称单词，导致在原文中找不到对应目标。

句子 The sub-family Bovinae comprises most of the larger bovids, including the African bongo, nilgai, eland, bison and cattle.

Q6

解析 原文提到属于Cephalophinae亚科的duiker不仅吃草，还会吃死动物尸体（dead animal carcasses）甚至捕杀小动物，这就等同于用肉类补充饮食。

干扰 你可能潜意识觉得牛科肯定都是纯吃草的，从而忽略了原文特意指出的这个亚科极具特殊的“食肉”习性。

句子 The duiker of Africa belongs to the Cephalophinae sub-family. / Although mainly feeding on grass and leaves, some duikers – unlike most other bovids – are believed to eat insects and feed on dead animal carcasses, and even to kill small animals.

Q7

解析 原文直接把Antelope（羚羊）描述为长腿、跑得快的物种（fast-running species），毫无保留地对应了“通常能快速移动”。

干扰 这道题非常直接，找到fast-running就能直接选对，你只要小心别看漏行就可以了。

句子 The term ‘antelope’ is not a very precise zoological name – it is used to loosely describe a number of bovids that have followed different lines of development. / Antelopes are typically long-legged, fast-running species, often with long horns that may be laid along the back when the animal is in full flight.

Q8

解析 原文交代Bovinae亚科全都是非领地性的（non-territorial），意思正是它们不需要保卫特定的领地。

干扰 你可能是卡在了non-territorial这个词上，它指的就是“没有领地意识”，直接对应了题目中的“does not defend a particular area”。

句子 The sub-family Bovinae comprises most of the larger bovids... Unlike most other bovids, they are all non-territorial.

Q9

解析 原文在描绘体型落差时，用“一端是仅有25厘米高的royal antelope”这种表达来体现它是最小的物种。

干扰 你可能在一门心思想找“smallest”这个词，但其实必须根据上下文体会“at one extreme (身高仅25cm)”代表的就是体型最小。

句子 This diversity of habitat is also matched by great diversity in size and form: at one extreme is the royal antelope of West Africa, which stands a mere 25 cm at the shoulder...

Q10

解析 原文直接点名auroch这个物种目前已经灭绝（is extinct），精准对应了题目中的已经消亡（died out）。

干扰 你可能看到了前面的endangered（濒危）就想抄附近的词，但题目问的是“已经死绝的”，你必须找到对应extinct的auroch。

句子 The ancestors of the various species of domestic cattle (such as banteng, gaur, yak and water buffalo) are generally rare and endangered in the wild, while the auroch (the ancestor of the domestic cattle of Europe) is extinct.

Q11

解析 原文交代sitatunga长有外八字的蹄子（splayed hooves），这使得它能在沼泽地（swampy ground/wetland）上行动自如。

干扰 你可能定位到了sitatunga这个动物，但是找错了核心词，答案要求的是促使它移动的那个具体器官部件。

句子 ...while the sitatunga has long, splayed hooves that enable it to walk freely on swampy ground.

Q12

解析 原文清清楚楚地指出barbary sheep已经适应了干旱的沙漠环境（arid deserts）。

干扰 你可能会连着后面的高山（mountains）和极地苔原（arctic tundra）一块儿抄，但题目仅仅只问了barbary sheep住在什么样的地形里。

句子 Tolerance of extreme conditions is most marked in this group: barbary and bighorn sheep have adapted to arid deserts...

Q13

解析 原文提到pronghorn是Antilocapridae亚科唯一的幸存者（sole survivor），等同于题目要找的“唯一的现存成员（only living member）”。

干扰 你可能是没有理解sole survivor就是only living member的意思，导致定位到了句子却不敢确定填哪个词。

句子 The pronghorn is the sole survivor of a New World sub-family of herbivorous ruminants, the Antilocapridae in North America.
